The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.18,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that occurred on 04.02.2023.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 04.02.2023 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA44J6968 on NH150(a) near Aladakatte Village, at that time,
the driver SCCH-10 of Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB3883 came from opposite direction with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's Motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to Government hospital, C.N. Halli.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Tumakuru Hemavathi Orthopaedic & Trauma Cetnre, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient from 04.02.2023 to 07.02.2023.

He spent more than Rs.1,50,000/
towards medical expenses, hospitalization, food, nourishment and other incidental charges and as per the advice of the doctors, the petitioner is still taking followup treatment.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 56 years and was working as Clerk in private High school and earning Rs.60,000/ per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered disability and he SCCH-10 is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.
The petitioner further contended that, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB 3883.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to award compensation of Rs.18,00,000/ under various heads with interest and costs.
3. In pursuance of Petition notice, both respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court through their respective counsel and filed the written statement.

4. The contention of the respondent No.1 (insurance company) in written statement is as follows:
The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition is not maintainable and denied entire petition averments.

The respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB 3883 in favour of respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident, however the Haridasa Naik S.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151434725/
2 liability if any SCCH-10 subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: Further contended that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy by entrusting his autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB3883 to driver to drive without possessing valid and effective DL and also not possessing valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Further denied the involvement of the offending vehicle as well as actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Autorickshaw.

Further contended that, as per police documents the petitioner was riding his motor cycle in the middle of the road without DL and without wearing helmet, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the offending autorickshaw which was going on correct side of the road.
Further contended that, a false complaint lodged which is after thought and created for the purpose of getting compensation.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner SCCH-10 is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against it.
5. The contention of the respondent No.2 (owner) in written statement is as follows:
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petition is not maintainable and denied entire petition averments.
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petitioner who came on his motor cycle from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and he himself dashed against the autorickshaw.

The respondent No.2 has admitted that,
he is the owner of the autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB 3883 and the same was insured with the respondent No.1 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident and also the driver possessed valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against him.

SCCH-10 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 04.02.2023 at about 8.00 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA44J6968 on NH150(a) road and when he reached near Aladakatte village, at that time, the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA04AB 3883 came from opposite direction with high speed and lost control over the Autorickshaw and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down from the motor cycle and sustained grievous injury ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.18,00,000/ with respect to the injuries SCCH-10 sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 04.02.2023.
12.

According to the petitioner, while he was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA44J6968 on NH150(a) near Aladakatte Village, at that time, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA05AB3883 came from opposite direction with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's Motor cycle and due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries.
13. To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

Further, on behalf of the petitioner, the Manager of Medical Records of Hemavathi hospital examined as PW2 and got marked documents as Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 and also examined the Doctor as PW3 and got marked documents as Ex.P.19 and Ex.P.20.

Ex.P.1 is the certified copy of the FIR No.014/2023 of Chikkanayakanahalli PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that, I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA05AB3883 for the commission of Haridasa Naik S.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151434725/

On perusal of the aforesaid documents it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence by the driver of the offending vehicle.

. Further the as per wound certificate and discharge summary Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.8, it appears that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
17. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

The petitioner contended that, he has sustained Communited Lower third fracture right radius and other injuries.
He further stated that, he has taken treatment at Hemavathi hospital, Tumakuru as an inpatient from 04.02.2023 to 07.02.2023 and spent more than Rs.1,50,000/ towards medical and incidental expenses.

19. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.

Same reads as follows;
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following;
SCCH-10 Pecuniary damages (special damages)

20. Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the SCCH-10 petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.6.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained several injuries in the road traffic accident.

petitioner is entitled for actual medical bills of Rs.71,372/ and same is rounded off to Rs.71,400/
under the head of Medical expenses.

Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.20,000/ is awarded towards pain and sufferings it will be just.
If Rs.5,000/ is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it will be just.
23. The petitioner has contended that due to the injury, he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that due to the disability he has lost earning capacity.
In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW3.
Admittedly, he has not given any treatment to the petitioner.
PW3 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has suffered permanent residual physical disability of 36% to upper limb and 12% to the whole body.
SCCH-10 24.
The damages under the head of loss of future earnings will be granted on account of permanent disability.

25. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has vehemently argued that, since the petitioner is still working in the same institution and earning fixed salary, he is not entitled to claim damages under the head of loss of future income.

26. In this regard, it is relevant to refer the judgments reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in the case of Sri.Subash Vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and ILR 2015 KAR 2268 in the case of Devaraya V.
Nayak Vs SCCH-10 K.J.Santosh and Anr.

sentences.text: In the aforesaid respected judgments the Hon'ble High Court held that, when the claimant has continued in the service, the claimant cannot claim the compensation towards loss of future income.
Therefore, in the instant case, though the petitioner has contended that, he has permanent disability, the said disability will not result in loss of future earning capacity.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income.
27. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injuries, he cannot do his routine work as he was doing earlier.
As per the medical records it reveal that, he was admitted to the hospital and taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of four days.
Further the doctor has deposed that, the petitioner has restriction of joint movement of right wrist and difficulty in lifting the weight.
Considering the medical SCCH-10 records and the evidence of the doctor, this Court is of the opinion that, due to said injuries, the petitioner must forego some comforts in her life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.30,000/ is awarded towards loss of amenities it will be just.
28. PW.3 in his evidence has deposed that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
Considering the future medical expenses, I am of the opinion that, if Rs.20,000/ is awarded towards future medical expenses it will be just.

29. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;

sentences.text: REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA 05AB3883.

The respondent No.2 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.1, as such,
respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

On perusal of Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy copy,
it reveals that, the policy was is in force at the time of the accident.
31. The respondent No.1 has specifically contended that, there is violation of permit conditions.
According to them, SCCH-10 the permit was given to ply the offending vehicle within 5 Kms radius of Tiptur Town Municipal Limit.

The accident occurred at Chikka Nayakanahalli Town Limits and there is a clear violation of permit conditions and hence, the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation since the policy condition was violated.
32. In support of its contention, the respondent No.1 has examined the ARTO Tiptur as RW2.
RW 2 in his evidence has deposed that, the vehicle had no permit to run in Chikkanayakanahalli Taluk.
RW2 has produced the permit of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA05AB3883 as per Ex.R.3.
On perusal of Ex.R.3, it discloses that, the permit was issued to ply the vehicle within the area of Tiptur Town Muncipal limit up to 5 kms radius.
Admittedly, the accident occurred at Chikkanayakanahallli Taluk.

Therefore it appears that, though the vehicle had valid permit on the date of accident, but the driver of the SCCH-10 offending autorickshaw had driven the vehicle beyond the permit limit and thereby violated the permit conditions.

33. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that, the petitioner is a third party victim and though there is violation of policy condition if any, the insurance company has to satisfy the award amount and can recover the same from the owner.

In support of this view, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A.No.8345/2017 between The Reliance General Ins. Co.
Ltd., Vs Smt. Yallamma @ Ellamma and others dated 3 rd July 2024.

Ltd. & others that the defence raised by the insurer that, offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned, accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastened the liability on the SCCH-10 insured i.e. owner of the offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award

sentences.text: the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, even in such a case the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
35. In the present case on hand, there is violation of permit condition.

However, the petitioner being a third party, in view of policy and indemnity between the respondents insurer and insured and in view of the above principles, at the first instance the insurer i.e. respondent No.1 has to pay the Haridasa Naik S.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151434725/

Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative.
36. ISSUE No. 3:

For the aforesaid reasons on Issue SCCH-10 No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The petition filed by the petitioner under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,46,400/ with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.

The respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to pay compensation amount as awarded to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.
The entire compensation amount shall be SCCH-10 released to petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.

The respondent No.1 /
insurance is at liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner ofthe offending vehicle in accordance with law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence by the driver of the offending vehicle.
. Further the as per wound certificate and discharge summary Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.8, it appears that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
17. Besides, it is settled principles of law that in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.
This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained Communited Lower third fracture right radius and other injuries.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income.
Therefore it appears that, though the vehicle had valid permit on the date of accident, but the driver of the SCCH-10 offending autorickshaw had driven the vehicle beyond the permit limit and thereby violated the permit conditions.
34. It has been held by Hon'ble Apex Court in 2018(8) SCC Page 492 between Rani and others Vs National Ins. Co. Ltd. & others that the defence raised by the insurer that, offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned, accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastened the liability on the SCCH-10 insured i.e. owner of the offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award
35. In the present case on hand, there is violation of permit condition.
However, the petitioner being a third party, in view of policy and indemnity between the respondents insurer and insured and in view of the above principles, at the first instance the insurer i.e. respondent No.1 has to pay the Haridasa Naik S.R vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151434725/
